excerpts: The gap between "works in testing" and "works for real users" is where shadow traffic and A/B testing come in. This guide walks through how to set up both methods, when to use each, and how to combine them for safe, confident LLM deployments.

To safely test a new LLM in production, you first shadow deploy the candidate model by sending it live user requests without showing its output. Your production model keeps serving users normally. Meanwhile, the shadow model processes the same requests in parallel, and you log its responses for later analysis.

Shadow traffic testing gives you real-world validation without any user risk:
**No user impact:** Shadow responses stay hidden; users only see production output
**Real-world data:** Tests run against actual traffic patterns, not synthetic benchmarks
**Risk-free evaluation:** Compare new models against your baseline before any exposure

A phased approach reduces deployment risk significantly. First, run a shadow test to validate quality and performance. Once the shadow model meets your thresholds, proceed with an A/B test to measure real user impact.

excerpts: The gap between "works in testing" and "works for real users" is where shadow traffic and A/B testing come in. This guide walks through how to set up both methods, when to use each, and how to combine them for safe, confident LLM deployments.

A phased approach reduces deployment risk significantly. First, run a shadow test to validate quality and performance. Once the shadow model meets your thresholds, proceed with an A/B test to measure real user impact.

Shadow traffic testing gives you real-world validation without any user risk:
**No user impact:** Shadow responses stay hidden; users only see production output
**Real-world data:** Tests run against actual traffic patterns, not synthetic benchmarks
**Risk-free evaluation:** Compare new models against your baseline before any exposure

To safely test a new LLM in production, you first shadow deploy the candidate model by sending it live user requests without showing its output. Your production model keeps serving users normally. Meanwhile, the shadow model processes the same requests in parallel, and you log its responses for later analysis.

excerpts: The gap between "works in testing" and "works for real users" is where shadow traffic and A/B testing come in. This guide walks through how to set up both methods, when to use each, and how to combine them for safe, confident LLM deployments.

To safely test a new LLM in production, you first shadow deploy the candidate model by sending it live user requests without showing its output. Your production model keeps serving users normally. Meanwhile, the shadow model processes the same requests in parallel, and you log its responses for later analysis.

Shadow traffic testing gives you real-world validation without any user risk:
**No user impact:** Shadow responses stay hidden; users only see production output
**Real-world data:** Tests run against actual traffic patterns, not synthetic benchmarks
**Risk-free evaluation:** Compare new models against your baseline before any exposure

A phased approach reduces deployment risk significantly. First, run a shadow test to validate quality and performance. Once the shadow model meets your thresholds, proceed with an A/B test to measure real user impact.
citations.title: How to Validate New LLMs With Shadow Traffic and A/B Tests

executive_summary.description: A high-level summary of the findings and recommendations for achieving persona and workload realism in Jungle3 to prevent 'plausibility collapse'.

persona_realism_pillars.description: The core thesis on the multi-dimensional pillars required for believable persona realism, including named identities, owned workloads, activity rhythms, and contextual artifacts.

role_name.description: The name of the internal role, e.g., 'Intake / FNOL Clerk' or 'Case Adjuster'.

responsibilities.description: A summary of the key responsibilities and tasks performed by this role.

ownership_boundary.description: Defines the scope and duration of case ownership for this role.

handoff_points.description: Describes the typical handoff points where this role transfers ownership to another role or queue.

authority_limits.description: Specifies the financial or operational authority limits for this role, such as payment approval thresholds.

v1_internal_role_taxonomy.description: A detailed breakdown of the minimum viable set of internal roles for the v1 insurance-adjacent domain, including their specific responsibilities and handoff dynamics. Examples include Intake Clerk, Triage Analyst, Adjuster, and Approver.

friction_types.description: The types of realistic friction simulated, such as approval bottlenecks, evidence gaps, SLA lags, and misroutes.

quantitative_targets.description: The default quantitative targets and safe bounds for friction rates, such as the percentage of approvals delayed or cases misrouted.

stochastic_mechanisms.description: The underlying mechanisms for generating friction, including probabilistic triggers and statistical distributions for delays.

tuning_knobs.description: The configuration parameters exposed to users for tuning friction levels, including global toggles and presets like 'demo_safe_mode'.

excessive_friction_signals.description: The key telemetry signals and rollback criteria used to detect and prevent dysfunctional levels of friction.

role_name.description: The role for which the pre-seeded ownership is specified, e.g., 'Claims Adjuster — Junior'.

owned_portfolios.description: The types of artifacts and work items this role will own at launch, such as active claims, pending approvals, and draft documents.

target_counts_and_state_mix.description: The target count ranges and state distribution for the seeded artifacts to ensure a realistic workload.

activity_rhythm_and_timestamps.description: The patterns of activity, work hours, and timestamp distributions that imply prior human engagement.

prior_activity_traces.description: Examples of historical activity traces seeded for this role, such as comment threads, SLA touches, and reassignment history.

pre_seeded_ownership_specifications.description: Detailed specifications for the pre-seeded artifacts and workloads each persona should 'own' at launch to make the environment feel inhabited. This includes counts and states for open cases, backlogs, pending approvals, and draft documents for roles like Adjuster and Manager.

core_objects_and_states.description: The central data objects (e.g., Case, SLA Instance) and the state model (e.g., New, In Progress, Pending) that form the foundation of the handoff model.

routing_and_assignment_mechanics.description: The mechanics for routing and assigning work, inspired by systems like Jira and ServiceNow, using assignment groups and automation rules.

sla_tiers_and_calendars.description: The default SLA tiers based on priority (e.g., TTFA, TTR) and the critical requirement for business hour and holiday calendar support.

inactivity_and_reassignment_policy.description: The configurable policy for detecting and acting on inactive cases, including warnings and automatic re-queuing to maintain velocity.

auditability_requirements.description: The non-negotiable requirement for an immutable audit trail that captures every significant event for compliance and realism.

arrival_process_model.description: The model for case arrivals, using a Nonhomogeneous Poisson Process (NHPP) to simulate realistic time-varying rates like diurnal cycles.

service_time_and_effort_model.description: The mixture model (e.g., Lognormal + Pareto) used for service times to create a realistic heavy tail where a few cases consume most of the effort.

priority_queuing_and_aging.description: The use of multi-class priority queues and aging-based priority escalation to prevent starvation of low-priority items.

target_aging_distribution.description: The target proportions for the backlog across different age buckets (e.g., 0-7 days, 8-30 days, 31+ days) to ensure a non-flat queue.

validation_dashboards_and_metrics.description: The key dashboards (e.g., age histograms, Lorenz curves) and metrics needed to validate the realism of the generated backlog.

actor_type.description: The type of external actor being simulated, e.g., 'Policyholder/Customer', 'Vendor', or 'Regulator'.

rationale.description: The justification for why this actor is essential for a plausible v1 simulation.

interaction_channels_and_payloads.description: The channels this actor uses to interact with the system (e.g., Web Intake, Email, S3 File Drops) and the format of their data payloads.

behavioral_simulation_model.description: The hybrid model used to simulate behavior, combining scripted sequences with stochastic variation for aspects like response latency.

simulated_exception_patterns.description: Examples of failure and exception patterns simulated for this actor, such as late replies or submission of incomplete documents.

v1_external_actor_simulation_plan.description: A plan for simulating essential external actors in v1, such as customers, vendors, and auditors. Details their interaction channels, behaviors, and the recommended hybrid simulation approach (scripted schedules plus light stochastic variation).

orchestration_pattern.description: The hybrid architecture combining a deterministic state machine (AWS Step Functions) for 'golden path' scripts and a stochastic engine (Amazon EventBridge) for background activity.

reproducibility_and_time_control.description: The key levers for ensuring reproducibility, including deterministic random number seeding, a virtual clock, and an event-sourcing pattern for replay.

llm_usage_boundaries_and_safety.description: The strict boundaries for LLM usage, limiting it to non-sensitive, templated content generation, managed by a gateway with safety filters and cost controls.

observability_and_tracing_model.description: The strategy for deep observability, using structured telemetry and trace IDs to provide detailed views of simulation behavior in tools like Honeycomb or X-Ray.

failure_modes_and_mitigations.description: An outline of potential failure modes (e.g., LLM hallucinations, state drift, cost overruns) and their corresponding mitigation strategies.

content_and_document_realism_strategy.description: The strategy for generating believable content and documents (e.g., claim files, invoices, correspondence) using templating, redaction, and synthetic metadata to produce plausible artifacts without privacy risks.

identity_generation_and_communication_st.description: The strategy for creating believable persona identities, including names, demographics, writing styles, and interaction histories, while minimizing legal and bias risks through diversity controls and collision avoidance.

access_control_and_regulated_feel_framew.description: The framework for implementing access control, approvals, and auditability to create a 'regulated feel'. Covers role-permission matrices, maker-checker flows, sensitive-field masking, and immutable audit log requirements.

plausibility_observability_and_metrics.description: The key metrics, dashboards, and traces that signal plausibility and 'time to real' on day one. Includes first-look dashboards (aging histograms, SLA breaches), target densities, and drill-down capabilities.

preset_name.description: The name of the configuration preset, e.g., 'Demo-friendly', 'Realistic Ops', 'Stress Surge'.

use_case.description: The intended use case for the preset, such as sales demonstrations, proof-of-concept evaluations, or system stress testing.

parameter_summary.description: A summary of the key parameter settings bundled in this preset, covering friction level, workload intensity, backlog size, and role roster variants.

expected_behavior.description: A description of the expected system behavior and characteristics when this preset is active.

customer_facing_configuration_presets.description: A list of recommended customer-facing configuration knobs and named presets (e.g., Demo-friendly, Realistic Ops, Stress Surge) to allow users to tune friction, workload intensity, and backlog size.

core_abstractions.description: The reusable, platform-level components (e.g., Persona Model, Case Lifecycle Engine) that are domain-agnostic.

domain_specific_adapters.description: The pluggable, domain-specific entities that must be configured for each vertical, such as data schemas (FHIR), regulated SLAs, and privacy controls.

retargeting_configuration_layer.description: The proposed declarative manifest (e.g., YAML/JSON) that allows operators to re-target Jungle3 to a new domain without code changes.

plausibility_collapse_risks.description: Key triggers for plausibility collapse when porting to new domains, such as using incorrect SLAs or mishandling sensitive data like PHI.

prioritized_second_domain.description: The recommendation and phased rollout plan for the next target domain, identified as Healthcare Prior Authorization due to market demand and structural similarity.

ux_validation_protocols.description: The qualitative research plan, including moderated think-aloud studies with target users to measure 'Time-to-Suspicion'.

diagnostic_heuristics_and_red_teaming.description: A checklist of plausibility signals (e.g., consistency, temporal realism) for internal red teams to use for auditing synthetic environments.

quantitative_telemetry_plan.description: The core telemetry metrics and acceptable ranges for monitoring realism, such as reply latency distributions and contradiction rates.

experimentation_and_calibration.description: The plan for using offline simulation, shadow traffic, and A/B testing to calibrate behavioral parameters like friction and latency.

release_quality_gates.description: The proposed multi-stage go/no-go process for releases, incorporating automated checks, canary validation, and business signoff to ensure quality.

cross_topic_references.description: A summary of how persona and workload realism has significant knock-on effects on other research topics, including Domain Anchor (Topic 2), Synthetic Data (Topic 4), Event Generation (Topic 5), and Regulated Feel (Topic 11).

recommendations_v1_actions.description: Specific, actionable recommendations stating what Jungle3 should do in v1 to achieve persona and workload realism.

recommendations_v1_deferrals.description: A list of features and complexities that Jungle3 should explicitly defer past v1, such as full legal-hold workflows or fully autonomous LLM agents.

recommendations_biggest_risk.description: A statement on the single biggest risk if Jungle3 ignores the topic of persona and workload realism, identified as 'plausibility collapse' leading to user distrust and product rejection.
